commit.message:
docs: document ROCK 5B peripheral mappings and validation recipes

The ROCK 5B page lists the devices the machine models, but not where
the RK3588 peripherals live, which header pins carry them, which buses
are shared with on-board devices, or which windows are still
unimplemented.  Anyone bringing up a guest has to re-derive that from
hw/arm/rk3588.c, the Radxa pinout and the board device tree.

Add a "Peripheral mapping" section covering UART, GPIO, I2C, SPI, PWM,
SARADC, RTC, watchdog and timers:

- window and GIC interrupt for each controller, taken from
  rk3588_memmap[], rk3588_unimpl_devices[] and the RK3588_*_SPI macros
  and cross-checked against the RK3588 device tree;
- the 40-pin header connection of each controller, with the pinout mux
  names and the GPIO bank/offset numbering rule;
- the on-board devices that share a header bus (RK8602/RK8603
  regulators on I2C0 and I2C1, FUSB302 on I2C4, HYM8563 on I2C6,
  ES8316 on I2C7, RK806 on SPI2) and the mutual exclusions that follow
  from the pin groups;
- the modeling status per controller, so it is visible which classes a
  bring-up can exercise on rock-5b and which are still unfinished.

It also records how to check the map: modeled windows appear by name in
"info mtree", unimplemented ones appear as rk3588.<name> stubs and are
logged with -d unimp, and the existing rock-5b qtest covers the modeled
side.

Signed-off-by: Zifeng Su <2859049527@qq.com>

Merge pull request #51 from asymecat/docs/rock5b-peripheral-map
